subject: biology

moments.title: Anthrax
moments.body: A small-town country doctor isolates Bacillus anthracis from infected sheep and grows it in pure culture. He demonstrates the bacterium causes anthrax — the first proof of bacterial disease.
moments.takeaway: A country doctor proves a bacterium causes disease.

moments.title: Tuberculosis bacillus
moments.body: Koch identifies the tubercle bacillus on 24 March 1882, the day still celebrated as World TB Day. TB kills 1 in 7 people in Europe at the time. He wins the 1905 Nobel.
moments.takeaway: The cause of the era's biggest killer is identified.

moments.title: Koch's postulates
moments.body: Koch lays out four postulates for establishing causation: organism present in disease, isolated in pure culture, causes disease in animals, re-isolated. Modern epidemiology's foundation.
moments.takeaway: A logical framework for identifying pathogens.

moments.title: Modified postulates
moments.body: Koch's postulates have been modified for viruses, asymptomatic carriers, microbiomes. Molecular Koch's postulates (Falkow, 1988) extend them to virulence genes.
moments.takeaway: Koch's framework is updated but still active.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: TB still kills ~1.5 million people/year. The full bacterial pangenome is sequenced. Multi-drug-resistant TB and HIV-coinfection remain major challenges.
now.open_questions: Can we develop better TB vaccines and shorter treatments?

reflection: Koch demonstrated that a microscopic organism caused a major killer. Why is germ theory still resisted in some communities?
